newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Tel not concerned by BT/MCI merger.
newsitem.headline: HK Tel not concerned by BT/MCI merger.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd chief executive Linus Cheung on Tuesday was unconcerned about the impact of the proposed merger between British Telecom and MCI on it or its parent Cable and Wireless Plc.
"Major alliances -- some work, some do not," Cheung told a news conference. "Really we must not confuse activity with results. We are focused on results and we do not do a deal for deal's sake."
Analysts saw Cable and Wireless's 58 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom as the prize British Telecom wanted when the two British companies held their failed merger talks.
Cheung said Cable and Wireless itself was actively forging alliances, pointing to recent deals in Germany and in the British cable industry.
He also reserved judgement on the BT/MCI deal.
"Clearly it is a very good deal for MCI. I do not know if it is a good deal for BT, it remains to be seen," he said.
